result:
Inline and shared metrics on an experiment should no longer end up with the same identifier, either through promotion or through an update that only changes the attached shared metrics. I haven't run any tests or added a new one, so this is untested.

- **Promotion (`experiment_saved_metric_service.py`):** `create_saved_metric` now drops any incoming `uuid` and always generates a new one. A shared metric created from an inline metric's query no longer inherits that metric's identifier.
- **Update with only `saved_metrics_ids` (`experiment_service.py`):** when an update sends only `saved_metrics_ids`, it now checks the experiment's stored inline metrics against the shared metrics being attached. If any identifier matches, the stored inline lists are fed through the existing de-duplication, which gives the inline copy a fresh identifier. When nothing clashes, the payload is left as it was.
- **Agent guidance (`metric-configuration.md.j2`):** the "promote by creating a shared metric with the same query, then attach it" instruction is replaced. It now says to create the shared metric and attach it, and to remove the inline copy in the same update.

I left `normalize_query_for_write` alone because the legacy migration path calls it directly and isn't part of promotion.

If any existing caller relied on `create_saved_metric` keeping a supplied `uuid`, it will now get a different one. I only checked the callers of `normalize_query_for_write`, not every caller of `create_saved_metric`.
